reading.body:
Bain & Company is recorded here as a management consulting firm with no AI products, no litigation, and no other holdings.

The record is a profile and a stated position, not a portfolio. The firm advises on strategy, marketing, organization, operations, IT and M&A across all industries and geographies, and its only recorded material on artificial intelligence is an argument: that to justify the investment, AI must do more than boost productivity and will need to unlock new sources of growth and value.

That position matters because it is the demand-side view of the same constraint this site tracks elsewhere. If AI has to produce new growth rather than cheaper output, then the case for the data centers and power contracts rests on revenue that does not exist yet. A consulting firm is often where that case gets built or rejected, before capital is committed to buildings and generation.

What the data does not cover is everything that would test the claim. There are no client engagements, no named AI offerings, no numbers, and no dated events beyond the profile verification. It establishes what the firm says about AI and nothing about what it does with it.
